title: Trump says no immediate plan to strike Iran as a tanker is hit near Hormuz
dek: Trump said in an interview the US is 'locked and loaded' but may have no reason to attack, while strike plans as early as Wednesday were reported. Iran says a 'maximum deterrence' plan is ready.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
US President Donald Trump said on Tuesday that he had no immediate plan to resume strikes on Iran, even as one report said that the US military was ready to start a short campaign as early as Wednesday, and a tanker was hit by two projectiles near the Strait of Hormuz.

"We seem to be getting everything we want," Trump said in a phone interview as Americans voted in the midterm elections. "We're having discussions, and we'll see how that all works out." He added: "I'm ready, we're ready. We're locked and loaded if we need to go, but there may be no reason for it." He also said the US was "not really in a war" with Iran, and that he was unhappy that Iran's stockpile of enriched uranium would remain in place while talks went on, according to one account of the interview.

## Wednesday: strike plans and a new tanker attack

One report said that US Central Command was prepared to begin striking Iran as early as Wednesday, and that the military was ready for a short campaign, according to summaries in other reports. The White House has not commented on the report. Trump told reporters on Monday that he was not considering strikes after the midterms.

Iran said a "maximum deterrence" plan was ready against any new US attack and warned of an immediate response, according to reports. Mohsen Rezaei said Washington "must fully and explicitly address Iran's seven conditions" before the Strait of Hormuz reopens. A senior Iranian official told reporters that the two sides were still far from a deal, and that there was no deadline for exchanging messages through mediators. A Qatari delegation met Iranian officials in Tehran, and Qatar's foreign ministry spokesman Majed Al Ansari described the talks as positive, reports said.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations centre (UKMTO) said a tanker was hit by two unidentified projectiles in its engine room about 14 nautical miles northeast of Lima, on Oman's Musandam peninsula at the mouth of the strait, on Tuesday, according to reports. The vessel was not named, no casualties or pollution were reported, and no one has claimed the attack. A day earlier UKMTO reported another tanker hit by two projectiles about 72 nautical miles east of Ras Al Khafji in the northern Gulf. Iran's Revolutionary Guards separately said tankers using an "unauthorised" route had struck mines; those claims have not been verified.

China's foreign ministry, asked on Tuesday about possible US or Israeli strikes after the midterms, said "military means are not the solution", and called for disputes to be settled through dialogue, according to the ministry's transcript.

## Tuesday: Ghalibaf's warning

Iran's leaders answered reported US strikes on Qeshm Island with a mix of threats and openings to diplomacy on Tuesday, as Qatari mediators said they had put a new idea to both sides and expected answers within 36 hours.

Parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, who leads Iran's negotiating team, said in a televised speech that Iran was "ready for battle with its finger on the trigger", and warned that any US strategic error would open "a new battlefield in the war", according to reports. "The ball is in America's court to prevent war," he said. Hours later President Masoud Pezeshkian said "no one will benefit from this war" if fighting resumed, and that his government was still trying to resolve the crisis "through dialogue", reports said.

## What each side said

Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi said Iran "retains the right to legitimate self-defence" after the strikes, reports said. Mohsen Rezaei, whom one report identified as secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, called the US response to Iran's proposals "not convincing" and said the Strait of Hormuz would reopen only if Iran's seven conditions were met. Foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei said Iran was "not afraid of diplomacy" but approached talks with "complete distrust", and that any understanding required an end to the war "on all fronts, including Lebanon".

Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi praised the role of Qatar and Oman in a post on X and said Iran had no hostility towards Gulf Cooperation Council countries, reports said.

Ghalibaf also said senior commanders and Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei had met last week and decided on "a response without geographical limits" to any attack, according to reports. A Tehran daily reported that Iran had updated its "target bank" to include US support bases in Europe; that is a press report, not an official statement.

On the US side, officials described Monday's strike as a limited, defensive response after Iran fired at a US aircraft; Central Command has not formally commented. Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they downed two US reconnaissance drones south of Qeshm and destroyed an MQ-9 east of the strait. Neither side's account has been independently verified. Israel's military said "no" when asked whether it took part, reports said.

## The mediation

Qatari foreign ministry spokesman Majed Al Ansari said Doha remained "hopeful that there is still a chance for a deal". An unnamed Qatari official told reporters that mediators had proposed a new idea and expected feedback from both sides within 36 hours. Egypt's foreign minister, Badr Abdelatty, urged Iran to show "flexibility". US President Donald Trump wrote on Truth Social that "Iran wants a settlement, as soon as possible".

## Why it matters for India

India depends on Gulf oil and gas that normally passes through Hormuz, and Indian crews are among those most exposed to attacks in the strait: an Indian seafarer was killed this week when an Indian-flagged vessel was attacked off Oman. Whether the 36-hour window produces an interim deal, or the post-midterm escalation that Israel has reportedly pressed for, will shape fuel prices and shipping risk for India in the coming weeks.

## What happens next

US midterm results were coming in on Wednesday morning, India time, with Democrats winning early Senate races (see our separate report). Iran says it can reopen the strait within two days if its terms are met; Washington has not publicly responded to the latest proposal.
